explanations: terra: A covering lies over their sight after heart and hearing are sealed; exposed objects cannot produce perception when the receptive faculty is closed.
luna: This verse pairs the earth as a resting place with the sky as a canopy and rain yielding fruit, matching the section's contrast between ground below and sky above.

luna: The source section explicitly notes that the spring noun عَيْن also means eye; here one spring splits into twelve, making the spring-as-eye word audible in a scene of gushing water. | terra: Twelve عَيْنًا burst from the struck stone and each people know its drinking place, a worldly miracle in which spring water becomes manifest and apportioned.

luna: The signs listed here include the heavens and earth, night and day, rain, revived ground, and animals; their observable combination parallels the section's four-direction survey. | terra: Its catalogue joins created heavens and earth, rain-revived ground, dispersed creatures, winds, and governed clouds as signs for reason—the same move from visible world to understanding.
terra: The traveler is repeatedly told to look at preserved food, his donkey, and the bones as God raises and clothes them; an enacted resurrection is placed directly before the reflective eye.
terra: Abraham asks to be shown how God revives the dead, and the birds make that act perceptible so his heart may be reassured; it joins visible demonstration to inward certainty.
terra: The command to travel the earth and فَانظُرُوا see the deniers' outcome gives the section's free downward gaze a historical object: traces of moral consequence.

luna: This verse calls the creation of heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day signs for reflection, stating the contemplative response invited by the section's look. | terra: Creation of the heavens and earth and the alternation of night and day are signs for understanding minds, supplying the field over which the section asks sight to move.

luna: This verse says the reflective people think about the creation of the heavens and earth, continuing 3:190's invitation to read visible creation. | terra: Those minds remember God while contemplating the creation of heavens and earth; it states the thoughtful seeing that 3:190's signs and the section's questions seek.

luna: The source section's eye/spring root meets an eye that pours tears, تَفِيضُ مِنَ الدَّمْعِ أَعْيُنُهُمْ; here flowing water comes from eyes in response to the message. | terra: Recognizing the truth heard from the messenger makes their eyes overflow with tears; bodily eyes register inward perception rather than empty looking.
terra: قُلْ سِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ انظُرُوا sends the addressee over the earth to inspect the deniers' end, turning ground into testimony.
luna: The section's question asks people to read signs by looking; this verse says some see every sign yet will not believe, showing how an open gaze can remain unresponsive.
terra: Every earth-creature and flying bird forms communities like human beings and will be gathered to the Lord, joining animal observation to resurrection.
terra: The question imagines God taking hearing and sight and sealing hearts, then asks who could restore them; present visual freedom is thus a revocable gift.
terra: God shows Abraham the dominion of the heavens and earth so that he may become certain, a positive realization of the invitation in 7:185 to inspect that dominion.
terra: Abraham sees a star and tests whether a visible heavenly object can be Lord; its setting begins a disciplined gaze that refuses to stop at the object.
terra: He then sees the rising moon and again lets its setting expose the insufficiency of appearances, continuing the skyward examination begun in 6:76.
terra: The sun, greater and brighter, is subjected to the same observed rising-and-setting test, so even the eye's grandest object cannot be the final destination of sight.
terra: Abraham turns his face toward the One who originated the heavens and earth; it states where the created-object gaze of 6:75-78 is meant to lead.
terra: God splits grain and seed, brings living from dead and dead from living; the claim supplies the hidden creative action behind the fruit 6:99 tells people to watch.
terra: Dawn, night, sun, and moon are precisely measured, moving the same sign-sequence through the sky before it reaches earthly growth.

luna: This verse makes stars signs for finding one's way through land and sea at night, connecting the section's upward look at the sky with orientation on the earth below. | terra: Stars are made for guidance in the darkness of land and sea, assigning the upward gaze a practical as well as reflective direction.
terra: Humanity's creation from one soul inserts the observer's own origin into the visible signs that culminate in 6:99.

luna: The section asks readers to inspect created beings; this verse commands people to look at fruit as it grows and ripens, أُنظُرُوا إِلَىٰ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَا أَثْمَرَ, a deliberate gaze at provision. | terra: انظُرُوا إِلَى ثَمَرِهِ invites close sight of fruit forming and ripening after rain, making ordinary visible growth an intelligible sign rather than an empty spectacle.

luna: The source section cites a gaze directed toward the Lord; this ayah sets a boundary by saying eyes do not encompass Him, clarifying that directed sight is not exhaustive grasp. | terra: لَّا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصَارُ sets a boundary on visual comprehension while God comprehends all vision; it prevents the final gaze of 75:23 from being mistaken for optical mastery.

luna: The section's source gloss connects looking with sight and insight; this verse contrasts whoever sees with whoever is blind, making explicit the boundary between perception and mere looking. | terra: بَصَائِرُ have come from the Lord, so whoever sees benefits himself and whoever is blind bears it; this states the moral stake of perceptive versus empty looking.
terra: Winds, heavy clouds, rain, and dead land bearing fruit culminate in كَذَٰلِكَ نُخْرِجُ الْمَوْتَى, an indirect creation scene made explicit as resurrection evidence.

luna: The section names the Lord-directed gaze of 75:23; here Moses asks to see God and is told he will not see Him, while the mountain crumbles at the manifestation. It marks a boundary around the image of looking toward God. | terra: Moses asks أَنظُرْ إِلَيْكَ, is told he will not see, and is directed to the mountain that crumbles; present sight's limit, the mountain, and the promised ultimate gaze meet in one scene.

luna: This repeated account calls the water sources عَيْنًا and says twelve gush forth; it repeats the source section's eye-and-spring double sense in a concrete flow scene. | terra: The twelve springs repeat the stone-and-water scene while the cloud and provisions surround it, showing عين as a publicly recognized source.

luna: The section asks for a seeing that considers creation; here people have eyes لا يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا and hearts that do not understand, a direct boundary between eyes and perception. | terra: لَهُمْ أَعْيُنٌ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ بِهَا states the section's empty gaze in terms of unused eyes and places that failure among the marks of heedless creatures.

luna: The source section quotes this question about looking into the dominion of the heavens and earth; its close asks what report people will believe afterward, connecting observation with the surah's opening hadith. | terra: The question sends reflective sight into the dominion of the heavens and earth, then asks which report they will believe; it directly joins the world's visible order to the section's opening خبر/حديث.

luna: The source section quotes the dictionary example ينظرون إليك وهم لا يبصرون; this ayah says idols seem to look at the observer but do not see, directly distinguishing looking from perceiving. | terra: تَرَاهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلَيْكَ وَهُمْ لَا يُبْصِرُونَ is the section's explicit empty form of looking: eyes are directed at the messenger while perception never occurs.
luna: The source section's root ع ي ن names both eye and spring; this verse says eyes overflow with tears, making the eye itself a source of flowing water beside the spring-as-eye image.
terra: The question asks who owns hearing and sight and brings living from dead and dead from living; visual capacity and resurrection are traced to one provider.

luna: The source section contrasts reflective النظر with merely looking; this verse says some look at the Prophet but remain blind, so sight alone does not become understanding. | terra: Some يَنظُرُ إِلَيْكَ yet remain blind and unseeing; this repeated scene confirms the section's distinction between turning the eye and gaining insight.

luna: This verse directly commands, انظُرُوا مَاذَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ, to look at what is in the heavens and earth, the same open field of sight as 88:17, 88:18, 88:19, and 88:20. | terra: قُلِ انظُرُوا مَاذَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ sends the same present gaze through both upper and lower fields named in 88:18-20.

luna: The source section develops the eye as the organ of gaze; here Jacob's eyes turn white from grief, a specific loss of sight that contrasts with the gaze still available before the Day. | terra: Jacob's eyes turn white from grief as he suppresses sorrow; the physical eye named by عين loses sight through suffering, unlike the freely ranging eye of the section.
terra: When the bearer of good news casts the shirt over Jacob's face, he becomes seeing again; restored sight makes the organ's vulnerability and gift palpable.
terra: People pass by many signs in heavens and earth while turning away; the whole visual field is available, but their stance empties the gaze of attention.
terra: The question asks whether they have traveled the earth and looked at former peoples' outcome, setting historical seeing beside the final abode promised to the mindful.
terra: God raised the heavens without visible pillars and subjected sun and moon; the ayah turns the section's upward question into a claim about what the observer can see.

luna: The verse describes the earth spread out with mountains, rivers, and paired fruits, then calls these signs for people who reflect, matching the section's earth-and-mountain view. | terra: God spread the earth, placed mountains and rivers, and made paired fruits; it closely restages the section's frontward and downward objects after 13:2's sky.
terra: Adjacent plots and varied gardens watered by one water are declared signs for reason, demanding discriminating sight rather than mere surface looking.

luna: The section's downcast gaze meets its reversal in تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ: on the promised Day eyes stare in terror rather than falling toward earth. | terra: The warning fixes accountability on a day تَشْخَصُ فِيهِ الْأَبْصَارُ, another bodily fate of eyes when the present chance to observe and answer has ended.

luna: After 14:42 says eyes stare, this verse adds heads lifted and eyelids not returning; it sharpens the fixed, terrified gaze that contrasts with the section's lowered one. | terra: Heads are raised while the gaze does not return to them; this locked upward stare is the directional opposite of the section's ground-cast eye, yet both show sight stripped of freedom on that Day.
terra: Even if a gate in heaven opened and they continued ascending through it, the upward scene would exceed the section's invitation to look at the sky yet still fail to convince.
terra: They would claim their eyes had been dazzled and they were bewitched; it completes 15:14 as an extreme case of seeing without perceptive assent.
terra: God places constellations in the sky and adorns it لِلنَّاظِرِينَ, explicitly identifying the raised heaven as something made for observers.

luna: This verse says the earth was spread, mountains set, and plants made to grow in measured balance, gathering the earth-side signs the section presents. | terra: God spreads earth, casts firm mountains into it, and grows everything in measure, closely restaging the lower two objects viewed in 88:19-20.

luna: The source section's root ع ي ن names an eye and is heard in the spring of 88:12; here the same spring noun places the God-fearing in gardens and springs. | terra: The mindful are in gardens and عُيُونٍ, another secure Garden occurrence of the spring word whose homonym lets the section hear an eye.

luna: The section presents a gaze available for reflection; this verse warns against extending the eyes toward worldly enjoyments, a specific limit on free looking. | terra: لَا تَمُدَّنَّ عَيْنَيْكَ forbids extending the eyes toward transient worldly enjoyments; the section's free gaze is therefore free for signs, not covetous wandering.
luna: The verse names livestock as created for warmth, other benefits, and food; it gives a concrete human relation to the animal creation the section asks readers to inspect.
luna: The verse describes livestock carrying loads to distant places, a specific use of large animals that adds transport to the camel's created form in the section.
luna: The verse names horses, mules, and donkeys for riding and adornment and says God creates what people do not know; it broadens the section's view of animals made for human use.
luna: This verse lists crops, olives, palms, grapes, and fruits as signs for people who think; it supplies a specific plant field for the section's gaze at creation and provision.
luna: This verse adds night, day, sun, moon, and stars as signs, expanding the sky-side objects of the section's free gaze.
luna: This verse adds the varied things made on earth as signs for people who remember, continuing the section's invitation to inspect the ground.
luna: This verse says mountains were placed so the earth would not shake, and mentions rivers and routes, tying the section's raised mountains and earthly orientation together.
luna: Following the earth's routes, this verse mentions landmarks and stars used for guidance, joining the section's looked-at sky and ground to orientation.
terra: Travel and فَانظُرُوا at the deniers' outcome follows the history of messengers, so thoughtful sight reads destroyed communities as well as created forms.
terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا asks people to watch created things cast shadows right and left in prostration while humbled, joining free directional sight to visible submission.
terra: Every creature in heavens and earth, including the animals, prostrates without arrogance; it completes the shadow-prostration seen in 16:48.
terra: Rain revives earth after its death and is called a sign for those who hear, pairing the visible revived ground with receptive perception.
terra: There is an instructive lesson in cattle: pure milk is brought from within their bodies, directing thought through an animal's familiar exterior to hidden making.
terra: God brings people out knowing nothing and gives hearing, sight, and hearts so they may be grateful; the eye examining creation is itself a created means of response.

luna: This verse asks readers to see birds held in the sky, adding a specific creature-in-the-sky scene beside the section's camel and raised-sky view. | terra: أَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ holds an animal in the open sky before the eye, a close counterpart to looking at the camel below and the raised sky above.
luna: The source section's gloss for the sky includes what is above and shades people; this verse explicitly describes shade as provision within the created world.
terra: Hearing, sight, and heart are each accountable, so the present ability to look at creation is a responsibility rather than a neutral possession.
terra: Whoever is blind in this life is blind and further astray in the next; physical language becomes the boundary between present insight and final loss of way.
terra: Those God leaves astray are gathered on their faces blind, dumb, and deaf; this intensifies the section's lowered eye into total bodily and sensory abasement.

luna: This verse asks whether those who see the sky and earth's creation recognize God's ability to recreate people; it links the section's visible creation to return after death. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا asks whether the Creator of heavens and earth can create their like and gives them a fixed term, turning the cosmic gaze directly toward resurrection.
terra: Those given prior knowledge fall on their chins in prostration when the Quran is recited; 17:109 completes this bodily descent by naming increased خشوع.

luna: This verse says those who hear the Qur'an fall in prostration and grow in خشوع; it offers a deliberate, devotional lowering that parallels the section's downward eye posture while differing from shame. | terra: Receptive hearers fall on their chins weeping and the revelation increases them خُشُوعًا; voluntary descent before the Quran now answers the involuntary lowered gaze later.

luna: The source section's free gaze is directed to created signs; this verse sets a boundary on where the eye turns, telling the Prophet not to let his eyes pass beyond the believers toward worldly adornment. | terra: وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ forbids the Prophet's eyes from passing beyond those who call on God toward worldly adornment, setting an ethical limit within visual freedom.

luna: The source section names عَيْن as both eye and spring; here the setting sun appears to go down into a muddy spring, joining the eye's visible horizon to the water-source word. | terra: The traveler reaches the sun's setting-place and finds it setting at a spring; عين as spring and an act of skyward seeing meet in one perspectival scene.

luna: The section's root ع ي ن names the eye and its gaze; here eyes are covered from God's reminder, a concrete case where physical eyes fail to receive what is shown. | terra: Their eyes were under a covering from God's remembrance and they could not hear, an inwardly blocked present gaze set against the section's open survey of signs.
terra: أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِرْ يَوْمَ يَأْتُونَنَا contrasts how sharply they will hear and see upon arrival with their manifest error today.

luna: The verse describes the earth as a bed, paths through it, and water from the sky producing varied plants; it gives concrete counterparts to the section's looks down and up. | terra: Earth is made a cradle with paths, rain descends, and diverse paired plants emerge, giving the downward gaze both traversable ground and signs of making.
terra: On the Day of summons, خَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ and only a whisper is heard; the root that lowers the section's eyes also subdues the whole auditory scene.

luna: This verse says faces are humbled before the Ever-Living, linking the section's lowered gaze to a broader posture of submission on the Day; its own contribution is the face's abasement before God.

luna: The section says today's eyes can still look before the Day when they are humbled; this verse reverses that present ability by saying the one who turns from remembrance will be raised blind. | terra: Whoever turns from remembrance is raised blind, making the section's warning concrete: refusing sight while it is free ends in a Day when it cannot function.
terra: The raised person asks why he is blind although he once could see; the question explicitly compares the lost present faculty with the state announced in 20:124.
terra: God answers that the person forgot His signs and is therefore forgotten that Day, explaining the blindness of 20:124-125 as failed attention rather than lack of exposed signs.

luna: This verse repeats the boundary on extending one's eyes toward worldly adornment; it makes the section's freedom to look a responsibility about what draws the gaze. | terra: The command not to extend both eyes toward the flower of worldly life bounds the present gaze by purpose and contrasts passing spectacle with the Lord's lasting provision.
terra: The heavens and earth are presented as once joined and then parted, and all life made from water; أَفَلَا يُؤْمِنُونَ demands belief from visible creation.

luna: This verse says mountains were set in the earth and paths made through them, then describes the sky as a protected roof; it combines the section's upward and downward field. | terra: Firm mountains and broad paths are placed in earth so people may be guided, continuing 21:30's created landscape and matching 88's mountain and spread ground.

luna: The source section defines the sky by what is above and shades; this verse calls it a protected ceiling, while people turn away from its signs, a specific boundary on the gaze. | terra: The sky is a protected roof, yet وَهُمْ عَنْ آيَاتِهَا مُعْرِضُونَ; the object stands open above while viewers turn away, the failure targeted by the section's question.
terra: Night, day, sun, and moon each swim in an orbit, extending the protected sky of 21:32 from fixed roof to ordered motion.

luna: The section shows eyes lowered on the Day; here the disbelievers' eyes are fixed wide in fear, شَاخِصَةٌ أَبْصَارُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, an opposite posture. | terra: At the suddenly near true promise, the disbelievers' eyes are fixed in a stare; the section's lowered eye and this transfixed eye mark different forms of compelled Last-Day vision.
terra: For doubt about resurrection, the ayah directs attention to human formation and to barren earth that stirs and grows after rain, joining created body and reviving ground.
terra: Because of the visible creation and earth-revival in 22:5, this ayah concludes that God is truth and gives life to the dead.
terra: The proof of 22:5-6 culminates in the Hour and God's raising those in graves, linking today's observed ground to the humbled eyes emerging from it.

luna: This ayah's observed order includes heavens, earth, sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, animals, and people; it gathers the same sky, mountain, earth, and creature field as the section. | terra: Heavens, earth, sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, creatures, and many people prostrate; the landscape of the section already bends willingly, while punishment falls on many who do not.
luna: This verse names sacrificial camels as signs from God and tells people to mention His name over them; it adds a ritual use to the camel the section makes an object of attention.

luna: The section's thoughtful looking joins eye and insight; this verse says blindness is in hearts, not the eyes, distinguishing bodily sight from the perception its question demands. | terra: Travel over the earth should produce hearts that understand and ears that hear; فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصَارُ locates failed vision in blind hearts, precisely explaining how one can look without seeing.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع is glossed through a gaze lowered to earth; this verse uses that root for humility in prayer, a devotional counterpart to the humbled gaze, though it does not itself mention the eyes. | terra: The believers are خَاشِعُونَ in prayer by choice, giving the root a present form of inward attentiveness opposite eschatological humiliation.

luna: This verse calls livestock a lesson and describes drink from their bellies and other benefits; it offers a concrete animal scene beside the camel selected for observation. | terra: Cattle contain a lesson, drink, benefits, and food; their created usefulness is itself offered for contemplation, closely paralleling the camel's invitation.

luna: The source section's water definition for the root ع ي ن is water apparent to eyes; this verse's مَعِين is a spring beside a settled height, a clear counterpart to that visible-water sense. | terra: Mary and her son are sheltered on a settled height with مَعِينٍ, a worldly instance of the section's dictionary form for water visibly flowing.
terra: God produced people and made hearing, eyes, and hearts, but little thanks follows; visual ability is created equipment whose intended response is named.

luna: The source section's lowered gaze is forced by the coming Day; here يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ commands men to lower their eyes now, making deliberate restraint a present counterpart. | terra: Believing men are commanded يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ; voluntary ethical lowering now distinguishes disciplined vision from the humiliating lowered eyes of the Last Day.

luna: The same root-and-eye detail appears in يَغْضُضْنَ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِنَّ: women are told to lower their gaze by choice, a present boundary beside the section's humbled gaze in judgment. | terra: Believing women receive the same command to lower their sight, confirming that a constrained gaze can be chosen purity rather than imposed disgrace.
terra: The feared Day تَتَقَلَّبُ فِيهِ الْقُلُوبُ وَالْأَبْصَارُ makes both heart and eyesight overturn, joining the section's physical and inward senses of vision.
terra: أَلَمْ تَرَ asks the viewer to recognize every being's glorification, with birds spreading wings in the sky; perception must reach the act expressed by the visible form.
terra: أَلَمْ تَرَ follows clouds as they are driven, joined, heaped, and release rain and hail from above, training the mobile gaze in a staged natural process.
terra: God turns night and day, and إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَعِبْرَةً لِّأُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ states that eyes should cross from alternation to lesson.
terra: God creates every creature from water and varies its movement on belly, two legs, or four; this is a direct analogue to considering how the camel's form was created.
terra: Those gathered on their faces toward Hell are called worst in place and way, a Last-Day reversal of today's upright, ranging observation.
luna: The source section's gloss for the sky mentions what shades; this verse asks the reader to see how God extends the shade and makes the sun a guide.
luna: After 25:45 shows the stretched shade, this verse describes its gradual withdrawal, making the relation between sky-light and ground visible.
terra: When reminded of their Lord's signs, the faithful do not fall upon them deaf and blind; their receptive response is the opposite of eyes directed without insight.

luna: The source section hears eye within the spring noun; this verse shows gardens and springs among what Pharaoh's people leave behind, giving the spring word a worldly, passing scene. | terra: Pharaoh's people are removed from جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ; the familiar garden-and-spring pair becomes a lost possession rather than the secure afterlife spring of the section.

luna: The source section names the eye-and-spring relation; here gardens and springs form part of the material prosperity of the people of ʿAd. | terra: The people of Hud are reminded of gardens and springs among their worldly supports; the same scene becomes evidence of provision that denial can forfeit.

luna: The source section's spring word echoes here in gardens and springs among the crops and palms, a concrete scene of provision from the land. | terra: Salih's people are asked whether they expect to remain secure among gardens and springs, exposing the impermanence of a worldly landscape resembling Garden ease.
luna: The verse asks who made heavens and earth and sent rain to grow a beautiful garden; it gives a specific created landscape for the section's reflective gaze.
terra: The command to walk the earth and inspect the criminals' outcome uses the same active, mobile gaze but directs it toward moral history.
terra: The viewer sees mountains and supposes them fixed while they pass like clouds; God's perfected workmanship corrects a confident surface judgment about the very object faced in 88:19.

luna: This verse asks whether people see that God begins creation and repeats it; the next 29:20 adds travel across the earth to inspect how creation began, tying visible creation to return. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا كَيْفَ يُبْدِئُ اللَّهُ الْخَلْقَ asks people to perceive creation and repetition; 29:20 then tells them to walk the earth and inspect that beginning.

luna: The section quotes the command to travel the earth and see how creation began; this verse explicitly joins that looking to God's later creation, making observation evidence for resurrection. | terra: The command to travel the earth and فَانظُرُوا كَيْفَ بَدَأَ الْخَلْقَ turns present observation of creation into evidence for the final creation, exactly the bridge developed in the section.
terra: أَوَلَمْ يَتَفَكَّرُوا فِي أَنفُسِهِم asks for inward reflection on heavens, earth, truth, and a fixed term, articulating the thought that must accompany the section's looking.
terra: أَوَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا contrasts the greater works and cultivation of earlier peoples with the ruins their wrongdoing produced.

luna: This verse joins life emerging from death to earth revived after death and says people will be brought forth likewise, a specific earth-and-resurrection parallel to the section's gaze. | terra: God brings living from dead and dead from living, revives earth after death, and says that likewise people will be brought out.

luna: This verse names lightning and rain from the sky and the revival of earth as signs, a concrete upward-and-downward scene for attentive sight. | terra: Lightning, hope and fear, rain, and revived earth are signs for people who understand, joining upward sight and downward life in one observable process.
luna: This verse says heavens and earth stand by God's command and that people will emerge from earth, linking the observed cosmos to resurrection.
terra: Travel and inspection reveal the outcome of earlier polytheists; the earth below retains evidence for a gaze willing to move through it.

luna: Before 30:50 tells people to look at God's mercy in reviving earth, this verse contributes the winds, clouds, and rain that make the land revive. | terra: The winds raise clouds, God spreads and fragments them, and rain comes through; this is the visible mercy whose آثار 30:50 tells the reader to inspect.
terra: People had been in despair immediately before the rain; the change supplies the human before-and-after against which 30:50 calls the new life آثار الرحمة.

luna: The section quotes this command to look at God's mercy in reviving earth after its death; the visible return of life makes the gaze a sign of the later return. | terra: فَانظُرْ إِلَى آثَارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ asks the eye to watch dead earth revive and explicitly concludes that its reviver raises the dead.
luna: After 30:50's revived earth, this verse adds the contrary sight of vegetation yellowing after a wind; it also says the viewers remain ungrateful.

luna: The verse joins skies without visible supports, mountains set in the earth, and creatures spread across it, matching several directions of the section's creation-gaze. | terra: The ayah gathers heavens raised without visible supports, mountains cast into earth, dispersed animals, rain, and plants—nearly the whole landscape traversed by 88:17-20.
terra: After forming and breathing spirit into the human, God gives hearing, eyes, and hearts; the viewer's eye belongs to the very created form it investigates.
terra: The guilty lower their heads before their Lord and say that they now see and hear; their too-late perception embodies the section's warning that today's mobile gaze will not remain available.

luna: The section sets humbled faces against the surah's promised ease; this verse calls the hidden reward قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ, a specific afterlife reversal from eyes lowered in disgrace to delight. | terra: No soul knows what قُرَّةِ أَعْيُنٍ is hidden as reward; the eye that can inspect present signs cannot yet see the Garden joy prepared for it.
terra: At the siege, eyes swerve and hearts reach throats; earthly terror already shows sight displaced from calm, deliberate movement.
terra: In fear, eyes rotate like those of one fainting from death; the bodily distortion offers a worldly foretaste of the eye losing its free movement.

luna: The source section's root ع ي ن links eye and spring; here سليمان is given an عَيْنَ الْقِطْرِ, a spring/source of molten copper, extending the image from flowing water to a visible issuing substance.

luna: This verse describes winds and rain bringing dead land back to life, a visible earth-and-revival scene that supports the section's link between looking and return. | terra: Winds raise clouds and drive them to dead land, which God revives; كَذَلِكَ النُّشُورُ explicitly reads the scene as resurrection.

luna: This verse asks the reader to see varied fruits, then describes colored mountain bands; it brings the earth and raised mountains of the section into one observed scene. | terra: أَلَمْ تَرَ begins with rain and opens into colored fruits and differently colored mountain tracts, making careful vision range from sky to the section's frontward mountains.

luna: Following the sight of fruits and mountains in 35:27, this verse includes people, animals, and cattle in the variety of creation and says those who know fear God; the camel in the section belongs to this living field. | terra: People, creatures, and cattle likewise differ in color, and true knowledge yields fear; it adds the camel's animal class to 35:27's observed world and names the inward result.
terra: Traveling earth and looking at the stronger predecessors' outcome leads to God's unfrustrated power in heavens and earth.

luna: This verse calls the revived dead land and its grain a sign; the next 36:34 adds gardens and springs, so this ayah contributes the earth-revival scene beside the section's spring image. | terra: The dead earth revived and producing grain is called a sign, making what people eat a visible witness to life after death.

luna: The source section hears the eye sense in its spring; here gardens and date palms are set in the earth and springs are made to gush from it. | terra: God makes gardens in dead earth and causes springs to gush in it, joining عُيُون with the visible sign of revived ground.

luna: This verse asks whether people see that God created livestock for them; it gives a direct animal-creation counterpart to the camel the section invites them to inspect. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا asks whether people see that God created livestock for their possession, a close animal-creation counterpart to the camel question.
terra: The livestock are subjected so that some are ridden and some eaten, exposing the fitted relation between the animal's created form and human use.
terra: Benefits and drinks come from those animals, then أَفَلَا يَشْكُرُونَ names gratitude as the proper answer to seeing how they were made serviceable.
terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ الْإِنسَانُ asks whether the human sees that God created him from a drop, turning the viewer's own origin into the contemplated object.
terra: The human forgets his creation and asks who can revive decayed bones, stating the failure of thought that 36:77 exposes.
terra: The answer points to the One who originated the bones the first time, making first creation sufficient evidence for return.
terra: Fire produced from green trees supplies another visible reversal of states before 36:81 turns to creation of heavens and earth.
terra: أَوَلَيْسَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ asks the same creation-to-recreation question without naming the visual act.
terra: At one blast people are suddenly looking, another resurrection scene in which sight resumes only after the decisive summons.

luna: The source section's water-visible-to-eyes gloss for ع ي ن meets a cup of مَعِين here, a drink presented as flowing from a spring in the garden. | terra: A cup مِن مَّعِينٍ is passed among Garden inhabitants, showing the visible flowing source as a drink within the same afterlife ease.
terra: Garden companions are described as قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ; restrained sight here belongs to purity and ease, not the compelled humiliation of the lowered Last-Day gaze.
terra: The repeated قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ places voluntarily bounded eyes within Garden companionship, preserving a positive form of lowered gaze.

luna: The verse follows water from the sky into earth and shows varied crops growing and drying; it makes the changing ground a visible sign beside the section's spring and earth. | terra: أَلَمْ تَرَ traces rain into springs through earth, varied crops, withering, and debris; the whole visible cycle becomes a reminder for understanding minds.
terra: After the second trumpet blast, people are suddenly standing and looking; resurrection restores them to sight only within the compelled scene of the Last Day.
luna: Before 40:19 names God's knowledge of furtive eyes, this verse contributes the approaching Day, with hearts at throats and people in dread, grounding the hidden glance in judgment.

luna: The section's hidden eye-corner glance is reversed by God's knowledge of خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ: a stealthy look is hidden from people but exposed to divine sight. | terra: يَعْلَمُ خَائِنَةَ الْأَعْيُنِ names the furtive treachery of eyes; it sharpens the hidden side-glance in 42:45 by adding that no covert movement of sight escapes God.
terra: The earth-journey question points to stronger earlier peoples and the آثار they left, treating visible remains as an accountable record.
terra: The creation of heavens and earth is greater than human creation; this comparison explains why the section's upward and downward gaze answers doubt about return.
terra: God makes earth a settlement and sky a structure, then forms people well; the observer, upper world, lower world, and created form are gathered in one claim.
terra: God made cattle so people may ride some and eat some; the camel's observable form is read through the purposes built into it.
terra: Cattle meet needs in people's breasts and carry them alongside ships, extending 40:79's fitted animal-human relation.
terra: God shows His signs and asks which they deny, explicitly naming the livestock scene of 40:79-80 as something displayed for recognition.
terra: The repeated travel-and-look question shows that worldly abundance could not save former peoples, so observation must pass beyond appearances to outcome.

luna: The section cites the root خ ش ع for humbled eyes and a view of earth; here one sees the earth خَاشِعَةً before rain revives it, joining that root to the earth-and-revival scene. | terra: The viewer sees the earth خَاشِعَةً, then sees it stir and grow when water descends; the root moves from a humbled gaze to low, lifeless ground and makes visible resurrection through the earth itself.

luna: This verse says God's signs will be shown in horizons and within people until truth becomes clear, a concise statement of the outward and inward seeing the section stages. | terra: God will show signs فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنفُسِهِمْ until truth becomes clear, expanding the section's four-direction gaze into horizon and self.

luna: The section directly cites this image: wrongdoers shown to the fire look from a hidden corner of the eye, يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ. It makes the gaze itself a sign of humiliation. | terra: The wrongdoers are brought before the Fire خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ and look مِن طَرْفٍ خَفِيٍّ; it supplies the section's precise union of humiliation and a furtive, constricted glance.
luna: This verse calls earth a resting place and mentions paths through it for guidance, a concrete counterpart to looking down at the shaped ground.
terra: Measured rain revives a dead land, followed by كَذَٰلِكَ تُخْرَجُونَ; the landscape supplies a direct image of human emergence.

luna: This verse says God created pairs and made ships and livestock mounts for people; it gives an explicit use for the animal creation the section asks readers to consider. | terra: The Creator makes pairs and provides ships and cattle to ride, bringing created animal form into a wider order of transport.

luna: This verse specifies settling on the backs of mounts and remembering God's favor, a concrete camel-adjacent use that follows the section's question about the animal. | terra: Settling on their backs should prompt remembrance of the One who subjected them; ordinary riding becomes reflective seeing of fitted creation.
terra: The riders confess that they will return to their Lord, carrying the contemplation of cattle in 43:12-13 through to final return.

luna: The section's eye image includes humbled sight and paradise; this verse says eyes delight in the garden's provision, a specific afterlife reversal from the downcast gaze. | terra: In the Garden are what souls desire and تَلَذُّ الْأَعْيُنُ; this gives the liberated afterlife eye not only range but enduring delight.

luna: The source section's spring-as-eye word appears in the gardens and springs left by Pharaoh's people; the scene makes earthly abundance visibly abandoned and passing. | terra: كَمْ تَرَكُوا مِن جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ records gardens and springs abandoned by Pharaoh's people, a worldly version of the paradisal scene that cannot be kept.

luna: The source section's spring noun echoes in this promised garden scene, where the God-fearing are placed among gardens and springs. | terra: فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ gives the mindful secure placement among gardens and springs, directly reversing the abandoned worldly springs of 44:25.

luna: The verse says there are signs in heavens and earth, naming the same broad visible field the section directs the gaze across. | terra: The heavens and earth are signs for believers, directly matching the upper and lower objects to which the section releases the eye.

luna: The verse locates signs in human creation and animals spread through the earth, connecting its camel example to the wider created animal world. | terra: Human creation and the creatures God disperses are signs, adding the viewer and the camel-like animal world to the heavens and earth of 45:3.

luna: This verse adds night and day, rain, revived earth, and winds as signs, matching specific sky-and-earth phenomena in the section's panorama. | terra: Night, day, descending provision, revived earth, and changing winds complete 45:3-4's visible sequence as signs for people who understand.
terra: Hearing, eyes, and hearts availed the destroyed people nothing because they rejected God's signs; possessing the organs does not secure the reflective sight the section demands.

luna: The verse asks whether the creator of heavens and earth can give life to the dead, directly joining the section's creation-gaze to its Day of Return. | terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا asks whether the unwearied Creator of heavens and earth can revive the dead, an explicit inference from looking at creation.
terra: أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَيَنظُرُوا asks for sight of destroyed predecessors and warns of a like end, giving present mobility an urgent term.
terra: Those with diseased hearts look at the Prophet نَظَرَ الْمَغْشِيِّ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ; fear turns directed sight into the constrained stare of someone overtaken by death.
terra: Those cursed for turning away are made deaf and their eyes blinded, turning moral refusal into the loss of the very faculties needed to receive signs.

luna: The source section quotes this same question: look at the sky above and how it was built, أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ فَوْقَهُمْ كَيْفَ بَنَيْنَاهَا, an exact parallel to looking at creation. | terra: أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا asks the same creation question as 88:17, directing sight upward to how the sky above was built, adorned, and left without fissures.

luna: After 50:6 directs the gaze to the sky, this verse supplies the earth below: it was spread out, anchored with mountains, and made to grow varied plants. | terra: Continuing the upward look of 50:6, this ayah turns sight to the spread earth, set mountains, and growing pairs, closely matching 88:19-20.

luna: Continuing the sky-and-earth signs of 50:6 and 50:7, this verse calls them insight and reminder; it names the kind of reflective seeing the source section asks of its reader. | terra: تَبْصِرَةً وَذِكْرَى names the purpose of the sky-and-earth scene in 50:6-7: it is meant to produce sight and remembrance in a receptive servant.

luna: Continuing 50:7's visible earth, this verse shows rain from above producing gardens, grain, and tall palms, making the earth's provision observable. | terra: Blessed water descends from the sky and grows gardens and grain; it begins the visible revival that 50:11 identifies with emergence from graves.

luna: This verse continues the earth's growth scene from 50:9 with tall date palms and layered fruit, a specific visible feature of provision. | terra: Tall date palms with layered clusters continue the inspectable growth of 50:9 before 50:11 draws the resurrection conclusion.

luna: This verse completes the rain-and-growth scene begun in 50:9 by naming provision and revival of dead land as a sign of emergence, joining the section's creation-gaze to resurrection. | terra: After the visible rain and growth in 50:9-10, كَذَلِكَ الْخُرُوجُ explicitly identifies dead-land revival with emergence from the graves, joining creation-gaze to 54:7's procession.

luna: The section contrasts today's available gaze with the coming reckoning; here the veil is removed and sight becomes sharp, revealing what a person had failed to see. | terra: The covering is removed and فَبَصَرُكَ الْيَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ; Day-of-Judgment sight becomes piercing only after the present invitation to see has been refused.

luna: The section identifies the spring word عَيْن with the eye; here the righteous are placed in gardens and springs, making the same water-source image part of the afterlife reward. | terra: The mindful dwell فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ, reinforcing the recurring Garden setting of the section's flowing عين.

luna: This verse says there are signs in the earth for those certain; it directly invites the earthward attention of the section's gaze. | terra: وَفِي الْأَرْضِ آيَاتٌ لِّلْمُوقِنِينَ makes the earth below a readable field of signs, the point of the section's downward but unconfined look.

luna: After signs in the earth, this verse asks whether people see signs in themselves, extending the section's inspection of created beings inward. | terra: وَفِي أَنفُسِكُمْ أَفَلَا تُبْصِرُونَ adds the viewer to the earth-signs of 51:20 and asks directly why inwardly meaningful sight does not occur.

luna: The verse says the sky was built and expanded, directly extending the section's upward look at how the sky was raised. | terra: The heaven is built with power and made vast, a compact counterpart to the question how the sky above was constructed.

luna: This verse says the earth was spread out; its wording gives another direct formulation of the ground-side scene in the source section. | terra: The earth is spread out immediately after 51:47's heaven, reproducing the section's downward turn from raised sky to laid ground.
terra: أَمْ خُلِقُوا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَيْءٍ asks the human creature the creation question from the other side: whether they arose from nothing or created themselves.
terra: أَمْ خَلَقُوا السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ follows 52:35 by setting the viewer against the same heavens and earth and exposing disbelief as failed certainty.
terra: Even seeing a fragment of sky falling, they call it a piled cloud; the sky is visibly before them, but interpretation protects denial from sight.

luna: The section's gaze can turn freely across the world; here the Prophet's sight neither swerved nor exceeded, مَا زَاغَ الْبَصَرُ وَمَا طَغَى, a stated limit on a particular vision. | terra: The Prophet's gaze neither swerves nor exceeds its bound during the great vision, supplying a positive model of an eye both free of humiliation and exact in attention.

luna: After 53:17 defines the gaze as neither diverted nor excessive, this verse says it saw the greatest signs of its Lord; the cited ayah gives the object of that disciplined sight. | terra: He sees some of his Lord's greatest signs, completing 53:17's disciplined gaze with the true perception of signs that empty looking lacks.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع and its gloss of a gaze lowered to earth recur in خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ: people emerge from graves with humbled eyes, the same bodily scene the section draws from. | terra: The section's gaze cast to the ground is staged exactly as خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ: people emerge from the graves with eyes humbled, so free sight now is set against the resurrection procession.
terra: They hurry with fixed attention toward the Caller and name it a hard day; this supplies the summons and judgment to which the lowered eyes of 54:7 respond.
terra: The earth is burst into عُيُونًا in the Flood; the same spring word that marks Garden water becomes overwhelming judgment water, exposing the image's opposite potential.

luna: The verse says the sky was raised, وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا, matching exactly the upward direction and lifting described in the source section. | terra: وَالسَّمَاءَ رَفَعَهَا states that God raised the sky and established the balance, directly matching the upper object and action posed in 88:18.

luna: This verse says the earth was laid out for living creatures, an explicit counterpart to the section's view of earth spread below. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ turns from the raised sky to earth laid down for creatures, closely matching the vertical movement of 88:18-20.

luna: The source section's عين double sense appears in two running springs, عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ, a direct image of visible flowing water. | terra: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ تَجْرِيَانِ closely doubles 88:12's flowing Garden spring and makes the عين/eye word audible in another paradisal scene.
terra: Garden companions whose glances are restrained show that visual constraint can signify exclusive attention, a boundary distinct from furtive fear or disgrace.

luna: This verse repeats the root ع ي ن for two springs, now described as gushing; it gives a second, more forceful form of the spring flow named by the section. | terra: فِيهِمَا عَيْنَانِ نَضَّاخَتَانِ supplies the paired Garden's two gushing springs, preserving the section's spring/eye word while varying how water moves.

luna: The source section's water-visible-to-eyes gloss for ع ي ن meets a cup of مَعِين, bringing flowing spring water into the garden's drinking scene. | terra: Garden youths carry cups مِن مَّعِينٍ, another afterlife use of the maʿīn water the section glosses as open to the eyes.
terra: نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاكُمْ فَلَوْلَا تُصَدِّقُونَ opens a sequence of direct creation questions by making the addressee's own createdness evidence for truth.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ directs consideration to the seed of human life, beginning the concrete answer to 56:57.
terra: The question asks whether people create that life or God does, paralleling the section's attention to how a creature is made.
terra: Knowledge of the first creation should produce remembrance, explicitly turning origin into evidence after the intervening death-and-replacement claim.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَحْرُثُونَ redirects examining sight to the cultivated earth underfoot.
terra: The question whether humans make the crop grow or God does uncovers agency behind the field viewed in 56:63.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ الْمَاءَ الَّذِي تَشْرَبُونَ makes everyday water another object of deliberate consideration, resonating with the section's visible flowing spring.
terra: The question asks whether people bring water down from clouds or God does, connecting the drink in 56:68 to the sky above.
terra: أَفَرَأَيْتُمُ النَّارَ الَّتِي تُورُونَ continues the same disciplined seeing with the familiar fire people kindle.
terra: The question whether people created its tree or God did again moves from a handled object to its created source.
terra: God made that fire a reminder and provision, stating the cognitive and practical purposes of the object inspected in 56:71-72.

luna: The source section names خ ش ع for a visible humbled gaze; here the heart is asked to become humble at God's remembrance, shifting the same root from the eye's outward posture to inward reception. | terra: The question whether it is time for believing hearts to تَخْشَعَ voluntarily brings the section's future compelled humbling into the present interval when response is still possible.
terra: After declaring that God revives earth after its death, the ayah says the signs have been made clear لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ, naming the understanding sought by the visual questions.
terra: The unexpected expulsion leaves a lesson for أُولِي الْأَبْصَارِ, making visible historical collapse something people of insight must read.
terra: Every soul is told to look at what it has sent ahead for tomorrow; نظر becomes present self-examination oriented toward the Day before sight is compelled there.

luna: The section joins the root خ ش ع to humbled eyes and separately looks at mountains; this verse says a mountain would be seen خَاشِعًا and split from awe of the Qur'an, bringing those two image details together. | terra: A mountain imagined receiving the Quran becomes خَاشِعًا مُتَصَدِّعًا; the section's gaze toward the erected mountain thus meets the same root that describes the lowered face and learns what true reception would do.

luna: The section's free النظر is made literal in ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ: people are told to inspect the layered skies and see whether they contain a flaw. | terra: The viewer is commanded to return the gaze through the layered sky and ask whether any flaw can be seen, an exact enactment of thoughtful upward looking.

luna: After 67:3 orders another look at the sky, this verse says to repeat the gaze; it returns exhausted, giving the act of looking its limit and result. | terra: ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ makes the eye range repeatedly before it returns خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ; even free scrutiny ends humbled by the creation's integrity.
terra: أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الطَّيْرِ فَوْقَهُمْ directs sight explicitly overhead to wings spread and folded, joining animal form, upper direction, and sustaining creation.

luna: The section contrasts eyes cast down on the Last Day with a gaze free to inspect creation; this verse contrasts one walking face-down with one walking upright, turning bodily direction into a figure for guidance.

luna: This verse says God formed people and gave them hearing, sight, and hearts, but few are grateful; it ties the eye that can look to the responsibility to perceive. | terra: The Creator gives hearing, sight, and hearts, yet people give little thanks; the ayah places visual capacity inside the same creation argument as 67:3-4.

luna: The section explains the spring-related sense of the root as water apparent to eyes; this verse asks who could bring back مَاءٍ مَعِينٍ, visibly available flowing water. | terra: The question asks who can bring مَاءٍ مَّعِينٍ if water sinks away; the section's dictionary sense of maʿīn as water open to the eyes is placed against its disappearance underground.

luna: This verse calls them to prostrate and says they cannot; the following 68:43 contributes the humbled eyes, linking failed bodily submission to the gaze's humiliation. | terra: They are called to prostrate but cannot on the Day the ساق is uncovered; 68:43 then shows their eyes lowered under disgrace, so inability precedes the humbled gaze.

luna: The section's خ ش ع eye posture appears as خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ, with disgrace overtaking those who cannot raise their gaze. | terra: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ repeats the image of lowered eyes under disgrace on the promised Day and shows that the bodily gaze reveals inward humiliation.

luna: This verse has people rushing toward the caller; 70:44 then supplies the humbled eyes and disgrace, continuing the resurrection scene of the section. | terra: People rush from the graves as though racing to a marker; 70:44 supplies their lowered eyes, while this ayah contributes the direction and speed of the compelled movement.

luna: The source section's root خ ش ع is applied directly to eyes here: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ, as disgrace overtakes those facing judgment. | terra: After the rush from the graves, خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ names the same downward gaze and disgrace that the section opposes to today's freedom to look.

luna: The verse asks how God created seven skies layered above, repeating the source section's question about the construction of the sky. | terra: أَلَمْ تَرَوْا كَيْفَ خَلَقَ اللَّهُ asks viewers how God created seven layered heavens, a repeated formulation of the section's creation-question.

luna: Continuing the sky scene, this verse places the moon as light within it and the sun as a lamp, giving visible particulars above the viewer. | terra: Moon and sun are placed within those heavens as light and lamp, giving the upward gaze of 71:15 definite visible objects.
terra: God caused humanity to grow from the earth like a plant, joining the observer's creation to the ground being observed.
terra: God will return people into earth and bring them out again, making the earth-growth of 71:17 an explicit image of burial and resurrection.
terra: God makes earth a carpet for people, continuing 71:15-18's creation-and-return sequence with the ground's present usability.
terra: Broad roads through that earth explain how people may move across the surface they are invited to inspect.
terra: ثُمَّ نَظَرَ uses the section's contemplative sense of نظر for a hostile evaluator of revelation, showing that mental scrutiny can still be bent toward a false verdict.
terra: فَإِذَا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ portrays sight dazzled at the Hour, another precise loss of the calm, ranging gaze invited in the present.

luna: This verse describes radiant faces immediately before 75:23 says they look toward their Lord; it supplies the face's joyful state around the gaze named by the section. | terra: وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ supplies the radiant faces whose action 75:23 completes by looking toward their Lord, reversing the humbled faces of 88:2.

luna: The source section explicitly names this as the farthest destination of النظر: faces on that Day look toward their Lord, إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ. | terra: إِلَى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ gives the section's furthest possible destination of sight: radiant faces looking toward their Lord.
terra: The immediately opposed faces are بَاسِرَةٌ; beside the radiant gaze of 75:22-23, this ayah preserves the same two-face division that structures surah 88.
terra: The gloomy face of 75:24 expects a back-breaking calamity; this ayah supplies the anticipation that visibly shapes the face.
terra: The human was a drop of emitted fluid, beginning another answer to the question how a familiar creature was created.
terra: The drop becomes a clinging form which God creates and proportions, exposing the hidden sequence behind the visible human observer.
terra: Male and female are made as a pair from that formation, completing the first-creation account.
terra: The passage asks whether the One who performed 75:37-39 can revive the dead, drawing the same return-inference from how creation began.
terra: God creates the human from a mixed drop for testing and makes him hearing and seeing, joining bodily origin, visual capacity, and accountability.

luna: The source section hears eye in the noun عَيْن; this verse presents a spring from which God's servants drink and which they cause to flow abundantly. | terra: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ is a Garden spring whose water God's servants cause to flow abundantly, a direct counterpart to 88:12.

luna: This verse names a garden spring عَيْنًا and calls it Salsabil; it repeats the source section's spring-as-eye word in a paradise scene. | terra: عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلًا identifies another named Garden spring, extending the section's attention to عين as both spring and eye.
terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا asks about earth made as a container, another direct question about the prepared ground under the viewer.
terra: The earth gathers both living and dead, giving 77:25's containing ground a relation to present habitation and burial.
terra: High firm mountains and fresh water are placed on that earth, completing a close mountain-ground-water counterpart to 88's viewed landscape.

luna: The source section's spring noun echoes in the righteous dwelling among shade and springs, pairing its water image with shelter. | terra: The mindful are among shade and عُيُونٍ, adding shelter and accessible water to the Garden spring scene.

luna: The verse asks whether earth was made a resting place, a direct formulation of the ground made accessible to those looking down. | terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا opens another creation proof by asking about earth made as a prepared resting place.

luna: This verse calls mountains pegs, giving an account of their placement that complements the section's question about how mountains were raised. | terra: The mountains are made as pegs, completing the precise earth-and-mountain pair of 78:6 and closely echoing 88:19-20.
terra: Seven strong heavens are built above, adding the upper direction to the earth and mountains of 78:6-7.
terra: A blazing lamp is placed in the built heavens, giving the eye a familiar sign within the upper structure of 78:12.
terra: Abundant water is sent from rain clouds, beginning the visible provision that follows the earth-sky construction.
terra: Grain and vegetation emerge by that water, showing what the prepared earth yields beneath the raised sky.
terra: Dense gardens complete the inspectable sequence begun with earth in 78:6 and rain in 78:14.
terra: On the near punishment's Day, a person looks at what his hands sent ahead; the reflective act postponed in life becomes unavoidable self-review.
luna: After this verse's trembling hearts, 79:9 says the eyes are humbled; the cited ayah adds the inner dread surrounding the downcast gaze.

luna: The section names خ ش ع for eyes cast down; here أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives that posture at the Day of Resurrection, after the preceding verse's trembling faces. | terra: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives the same Last-Day state as the section: eyes themselves are humbled and unable to range freely.
luna: After 79:9 shows humbled eyes on the Day, this verse records the deniers asking whether they will be returned after becoming decayed bones, grounding the gaze in dispute over resurrection.

luna: The verse asks whether creating people or the sky was harder, opening a scene in which the raised sky, spread earth, mountains, and pasture are evidence of creation's power. | terra: أَأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ خَلْقًا أَمِ السَّمَاءُ answers resurrection doubt by asking whether humans or the constructed sky are harder to create, paralleling 88's كَيْفَ خُلِقَتْ.

luna: Continuing the creation question of 79:27, this verse says God raised and proportioned the sky, directly matching the section's upward gaze. | terra: God raised and proportioned the sky's structure, a close verbal and visual counterpart to 88:18 within the creation proof begun in 79:27.

luna: This verse completes the sky's ordering with its dark night and brought-out daylight, extending the upward scene from 79:28. | terra: Darkened night and brought-forth daylight make the raised sky of 79:27-28 visibly ordered before the passage turns to earth.

luna: After the sky in 79:28 and 79:29, this verse says the earth was spread out, matching the section's downward gaze to the earth. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا turns the same proof downward to the spread earth, corresponding to 88:20.

luna: This verse adds water and pasture from the spread earth of 79:30, giving visible life to the ground the section asks readers to inspect. | terra: Water and pasture are brought from the spread earth of 79:30, showing what the downward gaze can discern in that prepared surface.

luna: The continuation sets mountains firmly in place, matching the section's separate upward look at how mountains were raised. | terra: وَالْجِبَالَ أَرْسَاهَا places fixed mountains between sky and earth in the sequence, corresponding to the frontward object of 88:19.

luna: This verse completes the provision scene by naming livelihood for people and their livestock; it links the preceding pasture and the section's camel to sustenance. | terra: مَتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ closes the sky-earth-mountain sequence as provision for people and cattle, relating the viewed world to the camel's lived setting.

luna: This verse directly commands, فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ إِلَىٰ طَعَامِهِ, to inspect food, opening a close view of the earth's provision alongside the section's creation-gaze. | terra: فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ إِلَى طَعَامِهِ redirects the same examining gaze to an everyday provision whose making the next verses unfold.

luna: Following the command to look at food in 80:24, this verse shows rain poured down, the first step in the provisioning scene. | terra: أَنَّا صَبَبْنَا الْمَاءَ صَبًّا begins the process that 80:24 commands the human to inspect in his food.

luna: The food sequence from 80:24 continues as the earth is split open, supplying the ground-level scene behind the section's look toward earth. | terra: ثُمَّ شَقَقْنَا الْأَرْضَ شَقًّا turns the inspecting eye downward to the earth opened for growth.
luna: This verse continues the inspected food scene with grain, a visible product of the earth. | terra: Grain is grown from the split ground, the first visible answer to the food-question in 80:24.

luna: The next verse adds grapes and edible greens to the food grown from the earth. | terra: Grapes and fresh herbage diversify the products the commanded gaze is meant to trace back to their making.
luna: This verse adds olive and date palms to the same sequence of visible crops. | terra: Olives and palms continue the visible catalogue of provision produced through water and opened earth.
luna: The food passage continues with densely planted gardens, extending the visible growth scene. | terra: Dense gardens enlarge the viewed scene beyond a single item of food.

luna: This verse adds fruit and pasture, connecting the earth's growth to the camel and livestock in the section. | terra: Fruit and pasture join human food to the familiar animal environment evoked by the camel.

luna: This verse completes the sequence by naming provision for people and their livestock; it connects the observed crops to the section's created camel. | terra: مَتَاعًا لَّكُمْ وَلِأَنْعَامِكُمْ names the whole observed sequence as provision for people and their cattle.
terra: Faces that Day are radiant, supplying another half of the opposing Last-Day face tableau that structures surah 88.
terra: Those radiant faces laugh and rejoice, completing the blessed face-state introduced in 80:38.
terra: Other faces that Day are covered with dust, a direct counterpart to the humbled face and downward association of 88:2.
terra: Darkness overspreads the dust-covered faces of 80:40, completing their visible mark of ruin.
terra: The dust-darkened faces are identified as disbelieving and flagrantly sinful, stating the moral division expressed visually in 80:40-41.
terra: At the upheaval, prized pregnant she-camels are abandoned; the animal people are asked to inspect now loses all ordinary value when the promised Day arrives.
terra: The guilty are مَحْجُوبُونَ from their Lord that Day, a precise boundary opposite the radiant faces looking toward their Lord in 75:23.

luna: The section cites this raised, free gaze: people reclining on couches look around, عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ, a paradise counterpart to eyes cast down. | terra: عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ places the Garden's people on couches looking freely, the section's afterlife destination for an eye no longer cast down.

luna: The source section's عين means both eye and spring; here the close ones drink from a spring, عَيْنًا, placing that double sense in a garden of reward. | terra: عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا الْمُقَرَّبُونَ makes Tasnim a spring for those brought near, adjoining the same surah's couch-bound gaze in 83:23 and 83:35.

luna: The source section's couch-side looking recurs here for the righteous; set beside the section's fire-facing hidden glance, the same verb marks opposite destinies. | terra: The repeated عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ يَنظُرُونَ makes the believers' Garden gaze part of the reversal of earthly mockery narrated in the surrounding passage.

luna: The command فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ asks people to look at their own creation, closely paralleling the section's question about how the camel was created. | terra: فَلْيَنظُرِ الْإِنسَانُ مِمَّ خُلِقَ mirrors the camel question by commanding a creature to look thoughtfully at how another familiar creature—himself—was made.

luna: This verse gives the source of human creation as a flowing fluid, answering the inspection command in 86:5 with a concrete created substance. | terra: خُلِقَ مِن مَّاءٍ دَافِقٍ answers 86:5's command to inspect what the human was created from with an origin hidden inside the familiar body.

luna: Continuing the creation answer of 86:5 and 86:6, this verse identifies where that fluid emerges, making the human body itself an object of careful looking. | terra: The fluid emerging from between backbone and ribs continues the precise bodily origin that reflective sight in 86:5 is to consider.
terra: إِنَّهُ عَلَى رَجْعِهِ لَقَادِرٌ draws resurrection from the inspected first creation of 86:5-7, the same inference the section draws from created forms.
terra: أَلَمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُ عَيْنَيْنِ makes the two eyes themselves an object of the same creation question, so the instrument invited to inspect the camel must also be recognized as created.
terra: The oath by the sky and the One who built it condenses the same created upper object that 88:18 asks the viewer to inspect.
terra: The next oath turns to the earth and the One who spread it, preserving the sky-to-ground movement of the section.
terra: ثُمَّ لَتَرَوُنَّهَا عَيْنَ الْيَقِينِ moves from present heedlessness to unavoidable eye-certainty at the Fire, showing the terrible endpoint of sight that refused reflection.
